newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Drought ends but Namibian economic outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: Drought ends but Namibian economic outlook mixed.

text.p: Namibia's economy will be held hostage to the mixed fortunes of its primary sector in 1997, the Namibia Economic Policy Research Unit (NEPRU) said in its Quarterly Economic Review.

Good rains should spell bumper harvests but the livestock sector will not see an immediate recovery in output as producers restock after the recent prolonged drought rather than marketing their animals.
The Namibia Early Warning and Food Information Unit has forecast the highest harvest since 1990 with a total coarse grain output of 154,400 tonnes -- a jump of some 80 percent.

But despite an overall improvement in pasture conditions, NEPRU said livestock output remained low due to restocking in the commercial sector following a 16.8 percent reduction in cattle numbers during the devastating 1996 drought.

"Although the producer price for carcasses was 27 percent higher during the first quarter of 1997 than for the corresponding period in 1996, overall marketing of cattle was 75 percent lower," it noted.
An all-time high of 497,000 head of cattle were marketed last year.
At the same time the fishing sector faces a continued tough time following a reduction in fishing quotas.

Low fishing quotas had led to losses of N$130 million ($28 million) in 1996 and employment in this sector was down to 6,000,jeopardising government plans to employ 22,000 people in the sector by the year 2000.
Industry experts also believe that large scale rationalisation is inevitable unless government steps in with higher quotas and cheap credit.
Regarding the overall economic outlook, NEPRU said contradictory forecasts reflected a high degree of unpredictability of the output of the primary sector.

Huysamer Stals, the largest dealer on the Namibian Stock Exchange, has predicted a meagre two percent growth rate in 1997 due to a lack of economic diversification and the continuing strong dependence on South Africa, also experiencing a slowdown.

But the Economist Intelligence Unit in London has predicted growth of four percent. It bases its positive outlook on the end of the drought, an expected improvement in fishing conditions, and increased diamond and uranium production.
Both forecasts are well below the aim of five percent annual real growth under the Namibian government's National Development Plan.
On inflation, NEPRU said a double-digit inflation rate might be a reality by the third quarter of this year, if the upward trend in the rate for imported goods continued.
The annual inflation rate stood at 9.85 percent in April, down from 9.98 in March. Inflation for imported goods stood at 11.3 percent in April.
